nation wide union label campaign for augustin an official circular letter secretary treasurer john j manning of the union label trades department calls the attention of all international unions affiliated with the department to the fact that at a meeting of the executive board of the union label trades department on may 9 and 10 after a thorough discussion of the subject it was decided to conduct a nation wide campaign for the union label shop card and working button commencing august 25 and to continue for at least one month the primary object of this campaign is to instill into our members and sympathizers the urgent necessity of using our power of purchase to strengthen the trade union movement to aid fair employers in extending their market and to discourage hostile employers and associations of employers by withholding our patronage from them to make this campaign successful it is absolutely necessary that the department have the undivided support of the executive officers of the organization and that the rank and file of all j affiliated unions co operate in order that the greatest possible publicity and activity may be obtained as the first step in this direction the officers of affiliated unions are requested to communicate with the officers of their local unions asking them to have a committee of three or five members named for the period of the campaign whose duty it will be to agitate for the label card or button of their union when these committees are named the secretary of the local j union should forward this information to the secretary of this department in order that literature may be forwarded for use in j the campaign affiliated national and international unions should also issue litefature to be used by these committees it is necessary that the secretary of the department be noti fied if your union will co operate as suggested above in order that j additional methods to make the campaign a success can be put in operation the department may be notified under the following address 1 john j manning 202 of l building washington

economic highlights happenings that affect the dinner pails dividend checks and tax bills of every individual national and international problems inseparable from local welfarehas it failed has it been an unqualified success or has it fallen between these two extremes those were the questions that were being universally asked concerning the colossal recovery program when the first year of the second roosevelt s reign came to an end on march 4 there were as many viewpoints as there were speakers and writers one thing was fairly evident partisanship on the part of the press is still at a low ebb few republican papers damn the president as a matter of course because he is a democrat few democratic papers claim that his batting average has been 100 per cent most of the editorial comment reviewing the amazing year was measured reasoned realistic opinion on various major phases of the program runs about as follows national recovery administration the enthusiastic almost hysterical approval that came with its creation has abated it is given credit for bettering working and wage conditions for stabilizing certain industries for manufacturing a certain amount of employment for helping to correct such blots on the economic escutcheon as child labor and sweat shops but the gain in employment due to nr a has been less than was forecast and there is a growing fear that the tremendous weight of restrictions on business management in matters which have had nothing to do with labor constitute a dangerous trend toward fascism agricultural adj ustment administration this was one of the most extensively debated of the new bureaus when it started it remains so now secretary wallace s warning that continuance of our present policy of nationalism will require government licensing of every farm with government determined quotas and government controlled marketing methods and markets came as something of a bomb shell the farm problem remains as acute as ever income has increased but so has the cost of living and surpluses are still being produced in vast quantities opinion is about evenly divided on the wisdom of the government s policy of subsidizing farmers to reduce production civil works administration questionabie dangerous but necessary that is about the way much responsible viewpoint runs on this it carried 4 000 000 men through what might have been an inconceivably horrible winter prevented want destitution starvation some hold that it would be better and cheaper to simply have provided straight doles instead of largely manufactured jobs money this is where the administration s best piece of sleight of hand was performed it cut the value of the dollar to 59 cents and presto the treasury found itself 40 per cent richer economists are divided as to whether the results obtained will ever amount to much many regard the treasury gold policy as being unjustified and potentially dangerous taxatlon taxation is being used as a means of taking from them who has to give to them who hasn t in doing that it has thoroughly frightened business conservative opinion feels that oppressive taxation menaces recovery is likely to prolong depression liberal opinion still is working on the basis that equalizing incomes will offset any existing or potential tax burden one of the best summings up of all appeared in the united states news of march 5 listed as administration assets were restored confidence in the banks rapid liquidation of closed banks insurance of bank deposits up to $2 500 increased farm prices rescued local relief from breakdown built up navy saved property owners from foreclosure effective campaign against kidnapers better relations with latin america fixed minimum wages diminished child labor protection for business against cut throat competition revaluation of the dollar at about 60 cents revived faith of working population stimulated employment improved public confidence on the liability side the news lists largest deficit in history failure to provide comprehensive revenue getting plan for future the securities act stagnation of capital markets lack of coordination among government agencies repudiation of gold pledge wrecking of world economic conference damage done by gold purchase policy usurpation of powers of states government competition with business unfairness to aviation industry tragedy of army fliers revival of spoils system in public offices waste and scandals in cwa and war department purchases so there you are at the end of a year in which a slow insiduous and bloodless political revolution took place

our gas and electric light billsregarding these there is a little matter of importance to us all it is a widespread deep rooted impression that we are not getting what we have reason to believe is both due and right for us to expect is this true householders storekeepers users of electric power in fact the majority of us have noticed one unmistakable fact vet no public attention has been called to it san francisco and our trans bay cities need as much light as do other places such as new york boston philadelphia and chicago these latter compel electric light and gas companies to furnish as nearly as possible the illuminating power for which they pay with unvarying regularity at 8 o clock each evening our lights brighten up directly the theaters close with the same beautiful regularity they again become dim dim is scarcely an adequate expression for our 16 lights sink to soft yellowish glow with whose bilious imbecility even a common rush candle would blush to be compared we know electric light companies have a machine called the booster it is a splendid machine and does excellent work we love a good booster but a booster is no good if he doesn t work the electric light booster only works regularly between 8 and 11 and on extra special occasions we need a booster badly we suffer from any neglect of duty t yet we still continue to pay our bills month after month just as if tly booster were working all the time we pay these bills not because we get sufficient lights but because we have a meter the electric light company puts in for us and the dial of which is kindly read for us every month by some one the company chooses it is a matter of electrical units based on olson s law involving volts ohms and amperes by increasing the voltage the light power of our lamps is likewise increased that is what the booster does when it works on the other hand whether it works or not the amperes continue to rush through our meter and by their numberwe are charged our lights are no good without volts we cannot get sufficient volts without a booster we pay for light not amperes so we need the booster all the time why don t we get it because it costs the company wear and tear on a machine and the labor to run it another thing too most of us are absolutely innocent of all matters electrical i venture to say not one in every five hundred people using electric light has the faintest idea how we are charged nor in what way our meters are regulated we have to trust entirely to the company that puts them in the meters are placed in our places to show the amount consumed they are made to show the exact amount and can be regulated to register the exact nicety if they registered less than the right amount it is not likely the company would use them but if perchance they register more what then some folk have considerable doubt on that score now a meter can be altered to register more or less as required but we dare not touch it although the companies to which we are obliged to trust both can and do this matter of meter applies to gas and water as well if we connected an extra wire with the main incoming one we should be getting unregistered power thus to steal it would be a misdemeanor liable to the full penalty of the law rightly so too but suppose our meter registers more than it should is not that a like theft also that meters do sometimes register wrong is amply proven for gas companies will frequently change one on request and it is a common experience to find as a consequence the monthly bill has become materially smaller this necessary change takes time to accomplish one month at least two or three more generally and in case of mistake and overcharge during this period what redress have wer usually none if obtainable at all it is only with much time trouble and vexation of spirit worth far more than the actual loss itself corporations are arbitrary soulless concerns time was when honest men instituted such for honest purposes and the sake of economyi or it is in the little things and the small details of business so much money can be saved and made but corporations in their evolution began to breed a multitude of dishonest methods from which sprung the avaricious trusts yes it is the saving of a machine here or an extra man there and the trifling overcharges for as they tell you they cannot charge less these nickels and dimes it is that make those colossal fortunes which in recent years have grown to far beyond the comprehension of ordinary minds america is not the only nation that has seen this evolution the question of weights and measures was raised as stone tells us in england in the early part of the seventeenth century and legislation enforced to that end government inspection the state of new york has recently adopted similar measures what is our legislature doing that it has not done the same it is not necessary for even the state to pass law s relating to an official inspection of weights and measures or the regulation and registration of meters for the gas water and electric lights we are forced to buy from corporations our city fathers and our board of supervisors should take up the question they have the power and should be made to use it the inspection and registration of meters would be a boon not only to the people but to the corporations themselves for these latter would be saved from the practice of a systematic robbery they assert is so prevalent whilst the people w ould be freed from a suspicious doubt and harassing inconveniences existing so generally in connection with these lines of public utilities these fcts are thrown out merely as a suggestion to our city fathers it is a matter that must be taken in hand some day why delay action thereon any further why not do it now the result is bound to be good and everybody will say all is well percy m raymond

men and mules written for by george dawson i spent some time recently in one of the largest construction camps in the west this camp is famous for its efficiency it is looked upon by practical and upao date contractors as a model of its kind two kinds of animals are used men and mules there are about an equal number of each an officer of the society for the prevention of cruelty to animals would starve to death at this camp if he depended upon fees for a living cruelty to mules is unknown here experts are employed to see to it that they are given everything that is good for a mule first there is the food man it is his duty to inspect the alfalfa oats bran and other foods these must be of the best quality each bale is examined when it is opened to see that there are no rotten damp or decaying sections the oats are cleared of dust and the other foods are properly mixed the sleeping quarters of the mule are the best fie is housed in a clean dry tent or shed he is bedded down with new straw and this is changed every day during the night the barn man makes his rounds with a lantern to see that each mule is resting comfortably an expert farrier keeps close watch on the legs and feet of the mule shoes are carefully removed and replaced an experienced veterinary is always on the job to look after the health of the mule after a day s work if an animal seems unusually stiff or shows symptoms of lameness or overwork he is led away to a pasture where there is running water and green grass for a few days rest everything that is known to science experience and common sense is used to make the mule strong and healthy and to prolong his life this is what should be done with the men things are different they are housed in tents that are worn and rotting that are damp and uncomfortable when there is rain or fog the men furnish their own blankets the company supplies the straw but it is the straw that the mule boss will not use in his department the food is coarse and of a poor quality every economy is used in its purchase and preparation in warm weather millions of flies travel and swarm from the dung heaps and piles of offal to the soup pots and stew pans if the men need shoes the company has a supply on hand to sell for a profit no sanitary inspector goes through the sleep ing quarters of the men to see that they are comfortable if a man is worn out or gets stiff or lame so that he cannot step lively he is promptly discharged they want strong husky and efficient men men who will do the largest possible amount of work for the least possible pay and the least possible expense to the company if a mule dies or gets crippled his loss is felt if a man is crippled or quits or dies there are others waiting to take his place the boss telephones to the city and a trainload is ready men who have paid the employment agent money to get a chance to get a job these men are called wops yet these are the men who dig the tunnels build the railroads dam the water courses and conserve the nation s resources every hour of their toil is profitable to their bosses and beneficial to mankind when men return from war from fratricidal strife from a campaign of blood and murder they are welcomed as heroes covered with wreathes and medals and honored in song and story not so with the hero of labor and sodden toil he goes bankrupt with his stock of muscle shuts up his shop goes down to oblivion and perishes miserably some day the men who sell their muscle for bread will realize i and understand the importance and benefit of organizing and labor unions and when that time comes there will be compensation and consideration for toilers everywhere

a windowless factoryit will be a privilege we are told for toilers to work in a building without windows it will be the very latest thing in factories now building in fitchburg massachusetts it will be hygienically perfect we are assured no capricious sunlight but mellow uniform illumination by electricity no breezes hot or cold fierce or gentle but plenty of fresh air passing gently through the building lots of light and air but both under perfect control says a dispatch to the new york herald tribune award of a contract for industry s first windowless factory building a $1 500 000 plant entirely wlhout daylight and embodying radically advanced ideas for scientific creation of artificial lighting ventilation and other working conditions was announced in cleveland recently by the austin company engineers and builders the structure will be built for the simonds industries at fitchberg massachusetts it will contain five acres and will be one story in height simonds president of the saw company advised the engineers the decision to build at this time was based upon the confidence of the firm s officials that business recovery was near and their belief that present construction costs are favorable for immediate expansion against future needs the building will have solid sound absorbing walls its roof will have neither windows nor skylights illumination will come from hundreds of 1000 w att electric lights arranged to provide uniform light intensity which is rarely possible in daylight factories dependent upon the cleanliness of windows or upon the weather one of the many innovations will be the painting of machines in orange color to increase their visibility and help reduce accidents walls and ceiling will be blue green and white the ventilation system will bring fresh air to all parts of the structure after purification and temperature regulation cork pads will be used under heavy machinery and other efforts will be made to keep noise at a minimum production of three of the simonds factories one in chicago and the others in fitsburg will be concentrated in the new plant construction is now under way

safety effort cites intersection rulesgreatest danger in traffic lurks at intersections where 70 per cent of accidents occur launching a renewed effort to combat the threat of increased traffic deaths and injuries during 1935 the public safety department of the california state automobile association will center attention during january on the greatest point of hazard the intersection analysis of accidents says a statement by the motorists organization announcing the effort proves that caution at crossings of streets or highways is the outstanding requirement for safe travel too many drivers approaching an intersection gamble upon the chance that some other motorist will not be attempting to cross at the same time the statement declares many motorists are inclined to travel through intersections at an unsafe speed this lack of caution is particularly dangerous at blind intersections where the driver s view is obstructed in cooperation with local safety groups the automobile association will conduct a series of educational efforts stressing the need for carefql driving at intersections regard for the legal speed limit and for right of way rules at such points will be urged state law limits speed of fifteen miles per hour at any obstructed intersection defined as any intersection where the driver during his last 100 feet of approach does not have a clear view of all converging streets and highways for a distance of 200 feet along the intersecting roads or streets the right of way rule established by law is that a driver approaching an intersection shall yield to the one who has already entered the intersection when two cars enter at approximately the same time the driver on the left is required to yield to the driver on the right
